audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: both legs of the deciding quotation confirmed verbatim in copies we hold at the stated locators (Calderon 1908 printed p.10 = PDF p.20, page image re-rendered and read; Rogers 2010 pp.134-136, 161, 234 in the text layers). (2) Deciding source: a 1908 first-hand sketch (the only one that can exist for this lect, extinct c.1900-1920) plus a 2010 comparative-grammar dissertation that states the pan-Xinkan rule (stress on the last vowel before the rightmost consonant => final if C-final, else penult) and extends it to Yupiltepeque explicitly conditionally. Glottolog has no descriptive refs for xinc1243;org and Crossref lookups directly. (3) downloaded Sachse 2010 (LOT 254, open access): sec. 4.4.8 p.216 gives the identical rule V -> V́ / _C(V)# with citations to Schumann 1967:32 a

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.quote: 'In Xinka stress is phonologically conditioned and lies on the vowel preceding the last consonant in the word (i.e. V -> V́ / _C(V) #) (Campbell 1972a:187; 1997:166; see also Schumann 1967:32). Thus, Xinka reflects the common stress rule in Mayan languages ... The ALS confirms this rule inasmuch as accent signs are in most cases placed on the respective stress-bearing syllable.' Semi-speaker data show stress shifting to the vowel before the last consonant under suffixation (pula / pula-ka / tero-ʔ); 'According to the stress rule an accent sign on a final vowel implies the presence of a glottal
